nodes.name: Error Trigger
nodes.notes: SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written (again in handover/core-a/inputs/evidence-n8n-4.md, once, lines 49 to 51, 59: executions 6, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19 started with mode=error). This workflow ran once for every failed execution of the main workflow, but ONLY while it was published. Imported and not published, n8n logged that it 'is not active and cannot be executed' and nobody was told. So publishing this workflow is a required set-up step. One error workflow can serve many workflows; it is chosen in the main workflow's Workflow Settings.

nodes.name: Build message
nodes.notes: SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written, with typeVersion 3.4 (again in handover/core-a/inputs/evidence-n8n-4.md, once, line 49: the message held 'Workflow: hadavin-trigger ...', the execution link, 'Last node: Stop: refused or gave up' and the error text): the message held the workflow name, the execution link, the last node and the error text. Keep typeVersion 3.4: with typeVersion 3 n8n ignored 'assignments' and the message was null. The four field paths used here were all in what the Error Trigger delivered. Do not add the request body or any header to the message, and do not pass on the whole error object: its field execution.error.node holds the failing node with all its parameters and notes. The message holds no key and no event: the person opens the execution (the link is in the message) to find which event it was. The message never holds the document text.

nodes.name: Notify placeholder
nodes.notes: UNVERIFIED: what lands here by design for a 520 to 524 answer, for a run that ended in a state of the failing list and for a run still showing as running when the checks are used up (none of that was run, line 121), and for an execution lost in a restart (line 123). SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7 (handover/core-a/inputs/evidence-n8n-4.md, once each; lines 49, 51, 59, 122, 124): this workflow ran once, 0.047 s after the failed execution stopped, for a refused send (409, 401) and for refused events (executions 6, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19, mode=error, status=success), and it did NOT run when the receiver was down for about two minutes and then came back (case 5: three rounds of ECONNREFUSED, then success, execution 12, no error execution): a short outage that recovers is silent here by design. SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written (it does nothing). SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7 (handover/core-a/inputs/evidence-n8n-3.md, lines 90 to 95, once): when a main workflow had answered the caller through a Respond node and then ended in a Stop and Error node, this workflow ran once, 0.12 seconds after the failed execution began, with the message naming the workflow, the execution link, the last node and the error text; the caller still got the Respond answer (HTTP 200). NOT shown: whether this workflow runs for an execution that is lost in a restart of n8n (marked crashed): the test workflow for the lost wait had no error workflow set (lines 34 to 38 and 51 to 63), so assume nobody is told. Replace it with the client's chat or e-mail node and send {{ $json.message }}. What lands here by design, because a person must look: a missing business id or document text; a 401, 409, 400 or 413 from the trigger endpoint (never tried again); and a 502, 503, 504, 520 to 524 or no answer in every round of the main workflow's wait-and-sign-again loop, which means: not acknowledged; send again with the same key; it may already be running. Also landing here by design, since the state check was added to the main workflow: a run that ended in a state that is not a success (NEEDS_PERSON, DENIED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, ROLLED_BACK or STOPPED; the message names the state, never a reason), and a run that still showed as running when the checks were used up. For a run that was cut off by a crash or a forced kill this message is the ONLY notice a person gets today: Hadavin itself tells nobody. A short restart of the Hadavin worker must NOT land here: the loop waits it out.
